title:
An analytic is a type that implements the process function.  The type is parametrized with the
input and output types.  The input must be a type that mixes in DataFlowEvent and must have a
@dfe annotation.

The first parameter(I) is the Input to analytic, and the second parameter(O) is the output of Analytic.

The input must be a type that mixes in DataFlowEvent and must have a @dfe annotation which can be the metric result, or series of metric results, that will be evaluated by DFE.

The output defines the type of object returned by {@link Analytic.process} function.

An input to the analytic that is some type of DFE is required, but an empty output can be specified using “void”.
However, it is best practice to specify an output Type.

```type
@dfe(period="30DAY", interval="DAY", metric="ElectricityConsumption")
type MeterMonthDailyElectricityConsumption mixes TSDataFlowEvent<Meter>

entity type RevProAnalyticResult mixes AnalyticResult {

type ConsumptionOnInactiveMeter mixes Analytic<MeterMonthDailyConsumption,RevProAnalyticResult>
```

see {@link Ann.DFE} for how input instances will be generated based on data changes.
Implement Analytic.process/processSource in an idempotent logic. so the result should not change how many ever times it gets executed
with same input. Since  the order in which a data change triggered evaluation happens is not guaranteed.
data changes that can trigger an analytic evaluation are put into {@link AnalyticsQueue} to be processed.


No I/O should be done in the process function itself.  If fetches are to be done, they should
be put into the loadContext function (across all intervals for a source).  If objects are to
be saved, they should be returned from process for batch saving by the container.
Objects returned by process may be single objects, whose keys are generated by the container,
or an ObjMapp instance where the map keys are suffixes added to the generated IDs.

Alternately, extra post-processing may be performed per source object using the postProcess
method, although saving objects here is discouraged as well.

The flow of calls is as follows:
  loadContextAll
  for each source
    loadContext
    processSource
      for each interval
        process
    postProcess
  postProcessAll

The default implementation of processSource allows the individual
process calls to be inlined, removing the action invocation overhead.  It's also possible for
an analytic to override processSource with an alternate implementation that somehow operates across
all intervals at once.

If processSource is overridden, the new implementation must explicitly invoke process, or it will not
be called.
